The same internal restlessness fits ADHD and anxiety equally well
nodes.summary: Held open deliberately. Internal hyperactivity and anxious arousal are near-indistinguishable from the inside, they co-occur often, and depression/stress/sleep produce similar churn. Nothing in the record currently discriminates between them.

nodes.label: The evidence base doesn't obviously generalise to me
nodes.summary: The Horváth sample was 226 university students, 81% women, mean age 21.4, tested online without supervision. The authors themselves caution about generalisability to men and across the lifespan — so the dimensional framing is borrowed, not measured, for my case.

nodes.label: Is ADHD truly dimensional, or does it retain categorical structure?
nodes.summary: The dominant taxometric, quantitative-genetic and impairment evidence favours a continuum, but some taxometric analyses recover categorical structure within ADHD samples (Fassbender 2018) and reviews warn that dimensional thinking can license overdiagnosis (Kazda 2021). A clinically justified action threshold is still required. Held open on purpose.

nodes.label: Is adult-identified ADHD a continuation, a separate syndrome, or a false positive?
nodes.summary: Three birth cohorts found adult and childhood ADHD populations barely overlap, which would make adult ADHD a distinct syndrome. Careful reassessment instead excluded ~95% of screen-positive late-onset cases as better explained by substance use or another disorder, leaving masking-then-late-identification as the reading. All three possibilities bear on a first screening in adulthood, and the record cannot yet distinguish them.

nodes.label: Mind-wandering is impairing but may not be ADHD-specific
nodes.summary: The MEWS shows high sensitivity and specificity for ADHD diagnosis and mind-wandering adds impairment variance beyond core symptoms — yet an independent sample found no ADHD/non-ADHD difference and mind-wandering tracking anxiety instead. Small, underpowered samples on both sides; held open.

nodes.label: The internal state could be internalized hyperactivity or cognitive disengagement — opposite arousal poles
nodes.summary: Two named constructs carve the 'churning inside' feeling in opposite directions. Internalized hyperactivity (Weyandt) is a hyper-aroused, restless, racing pole on the ADHD hyperactivity axis; cognitive disengagement (Becker) is a hypo-aroused, foggy, daydreamy, mentally-slow pole tied to internalizing/depression. They imply different differentials — anxiety on one side, mood on the other — and nothing in the record yet says which the internal state actually is. Held open.

nodes.label: ADHD and anxiety co-occur, but the direction of the relationship is unresolved
nodes.summary: Given how often ADHD and anxiety travel together, three orderings compete: ADHD-driven failure breeds secondary anxiety; anxiety mimics/produces inattention that looks like ADHD; or shared temperament/genetics generate both. Reviews treat the temporal relations as an open substantive question, and the record cannot yet say which applies to the internal state. Held open.

nodes.label: Is emotional dysregulation core to ADHD or a correlated-but-distinct dimension?
nodes.summary: Shaw et al. frame three models that make different predictions: emotion dysregulation and ADHD as correlated but distinct dimensions; emotion dysregulation as a core diagnostic feature of ADHD; or the combination as a separate nosological entity. The evidence does not yet choose between them, which matters here because a foggy/churning internal state might be emotional dysregulation rather than the attentional core.

nodes.label: Self-report and informant accounts disagree, and which to weight is contested
nodes.summary: Sibley et al. found parent report more diagnostically sensitive than self-report, with ADHD adults underreporting and controls overreporting; Kooij et al. note that in adults the patient may actually be the best informant, while a collateral remains of great value. So the evaluation cannot simply trust one source — the discrepancy itself is informative, and the record currently holds only a self-administered screen.

nodes.label: Shared substrate versus distinct categories — where is the ADHD/autism boundary?
nodes.summary: The evidence pulls two ways at once. Genetics and neurocognition point to a partly shared substrate (pleiotropy, shared social/executive deficits), which would favour a common underlying dimension; yet the phenotypes differ enough that the field keeps ADHD and ASD as separate diagnostic categories. Both readings are supported, and this note holds the boundary question open rather than resolving it in either direction.

nodes.label: Is disturbed sleep a mimic of ADHD, a consequence of it, or a shared circadian mechanism?
nodes.summary: Three readings compete for the same observation. Sleep loss demonstrably mimics inattention (the rival view already recorded here); but ADHD is also strongly associated with disturbed sleep and delayed circadian phase, which could be a consequence of ADHD or a shared cause, and one review proposes the delay is itself the underlying mechanism for a subgroup. The rival, consequence and shared-mechanism readings are all supported, and which applies in a given person is not settled — so the sleep thread is held open rather than filed as 'just a mimic'.

nodes.label: Is low mood a mimic of ADHD, a consequence of it, or shared liability?
nodes.summary: Depression and ADHD share surface features — poor concentration, low drive, psychomotor and sleep changes — so low mood can mimic ADHD (the rival reading, mechanism:mood-disturbance). But ADHD also prospectively raises depression risk, with a causal genetic signal, so the depression can be downstream of the ADHD; and shared genetic liability is a third route. Which applies in a given person is not settled, and unlike a mimic that simply competes, the consequence reading means both can be true at once. Held open.

nodes.label: Is executive dysfunction the core of ADHD or one component among several?
nodes.summary: Barkley's model makes inhibition/EF the primary deficit of ADHD; Willcutt's meta-analysis finds EF deficits real but neither necessary nor sufficient, present in only a subgroup and not specific to ADHD. One frames EF as the disorder's core, the other as one route among dissociable pathways. Both are supported, so the note holds the question open rather than crowning EF the single cause.

nodes.label: The RSD label: helpful validation, or premature reification of weak evidence?
nodes.summary: The term rejection sensitivity dysphoria gives many people with ADHD a sense of recognition and connectedness, which has real clinical value. But the same critical appraisal that grants this warns that clinical use risks self-stigmatisation, framing the trait as innate and immutable, terminological confusion, and resting on limited empirical evidence. The pull between felt validation and scientific rigour is genuine, and this note keeps both in view rather than either endorsing or dismissing the label wholesale.

nodes.label: Candidate diagnostic marker, or a real but non-specific deficit?
nodes.summary: Time-perception impairment is consistent enough in ADHD that some propose it as a diagnostic characteristic. Against that: timing deficits appear in other neurodevelopmental and psychiatric conditions, the paradigms vary widely, and reviews still call for replication — so a real group-level deficit does not license an individual diagnostic marker. Held open, in the same spirit as the imaging and EF measures elsewhere in this notebook.

nodes.label: Is hyperactivity an impairing deficit or a compensatory behaviour?
nodes.summary: Excess motor activity is a core diagnostic feature usually treated as impairing and to be suppressed. But objective measurement shows movement predicting better working memory in children with ADHD, supporting models that cast it as a compensatory mechanism recruited to sustain cognition. Both readings have support, and which dominates likely depends on context and task — held open, with a direct bearing on whether restlessness should always be discouraged.

nodes.label: The romantic-relationship effect of ADHD isn't found in every sample
nodes.summary: Against the marital and young-adult findings, a college study found higher ADHD symptomology related to more social impairment and anger but not to lower romantic-relationship satisfaction or partner violence. The couple-level effect appears real but moderated — by severity, presentation (combined vs inattentive), sample and which metric is used — rather than universal. Held open as a caution against overreading any single relationship measure.

edges.quote: Adult ADHD was highly comorbid with many other DSM-IV disorders assessed in the survey and was associated with substantial role impairment.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). Nationally representative NCS-R evidence (N=3,199 screened) that adult ADHD travels with other disorders — the empirical basis for the comorbidity being real, not artefactual.

edges.quote: As many as 80% of adults with ADHD have at least one coexisting psychiatric disorder
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the open-access BMC Psychiatry full text (PMC5567978). Puts an upper-bound figure on comorbidity in adults; mood and anxiety are named as the most frequent.

edges.quote: approximately 25% of children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) exhibit an anxiety disorder
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). A specific ADHD–anxiety co-occurrence rate in children, from a review dedicated to the comorbidity.

edges.quote: Studies have concluded that emotional dysregulation is a distinctive attribute of adult ADHD psychopathology
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the PMC full text. Independent support that emotional dysregulation is characteristic of adult ADHD, corroborating Shaw et al.

edges.quote: the conceptualization of ADHD as a spectrum using a dimensional rather than a categorical approach to diagnosis and treatment has been proposed
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the PMC full text. Reports (rather than proves) the dimensional framing; cross-links this comorbidity note into the existing dimensional-structure cluster. Confidence medium — it is a statement that the view 'has been proposed', not new evidence for it.

edges.quote: The study of the comorbidity of ADHD and anxiety will be advanced through a more precise phenotypic classification of ADHD and the integration of research in adjacent fields such as temperament and genetics with current research on the psychopathology of ADHD.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Supports the claim that disentangling ADHD from anxiety needs better phenotypic structure rather than symptom counts; indirect (about research strategy), hence medium confidence.

edges.quote: emotion dysregulation is prevalent in ADHD throughout the lifespan and is a major contributor to impairment.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Establishes emotion dysregulation as pervasive and impairing in ADHD — the premise the 'core feature' reading builds on.

edges.quote: emotion dysregulation and ADHD are correlated but distinct dimensions; emotion dysregulation is a core diagnostic feature of ADHD; and the combination constitutes a nosological entity distinct from both ADHD and emotion dysregulation alone.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. The same review offers three competing models, so 'core feature' is one option among three — this is the honest counterweight to the supporting triple above.

edges.quote: emotion dysregulation in ADHD may arise from deficits in orienting toward, recognizing, and/or allocating attention to emotional stimuli; these deficits implicate dysfunction within a striato-amygdalo-medial prefrontal cortical network.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Gives the mechanism a proposed neuro-cognitive substrate — attention-to-emotion deficits — linking emotional dysregulation back to the attentional core rather than treating it as free-floating.

edges.quote: Overlapping symptoms between ADHD and comorbid psychopathologies represent challenges for diagnosis and treatment.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the open-access BMC Psychiatry full text (PMC5567978). Supports the 'not from the mimics' half of the hypothesis: shared surface symptoms are precisely why an instrument that separates ADHD from controls fails to separate it from its comorbid look-alikes. Medium — a general statement of the challenge, not a discriminant-validity measurement.

edges.quote: those who were randomized to CBT had lower IE-rated ADHD symptoms (p < .01) and global severity (p < .002), as well as self-reported ADHD symptoms (p < .0001) than those randomized to continued psychopharmacology alone.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch); IE = independent evaluator. RCT evidence that skills-based CBT reduces ADHD symptoms beyond medication alone.

edges.quote: Students with LD/ADHD must work longer and harder than peers, which makes managing time and productivity a critical skill for school success.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the open-access abstract. Names the effort cost — compensation means working harder than peers just to keep pace.

edges.quote: A linear mixed model revealed no significant treatment or treatment-by-time effects for the total AAQoL or its subdomains.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the open-access PLOS ONE abstract. Long-term follow-up found no added quality-of-life benefit from coping-focused CBT — the uneven-payoff side of the ledger.

edges.quote: Most studies find evidence for increased divergent thinking for those with high ADHD scores (subclinical) but not for those with the disorder (clinical).
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). The crucial nuance: the divergent-thinking advantage is a trait-level effect, not present in clinical ADHD.

edges.quote: The rates of creative abilities/achievements were high among both clinical and subclinical groups.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Real-world creative achievement is elevated across both clinical and subclinical ADHD, distinct from the trait-specific divergent-thinking task effect.

edges.quote: Adults with ADHD reported more real-world creative achievements.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Empirical replication of elevated real-world creative achievement in adults with ADHD.

edges.quote: Our findings suggest that goal-directed motivation may drive the enhanced real-world creative achievements of people with ADHD.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Attributes the creative achievement to goal-directed motivation — connecting creativity to the reward/motivation mechanism rather than a free-standing gift.

edges.quote: The meta-analytic synthesis of the studies to date found that sugar does not affect the behavior or cognitive performance of children.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). The core finding across 23 blinded placebo-controlled studies — no behavioural or cognitive effect of sugar.

edges.quote: Restriction diets reduced ADHD symptoms at an effect of g = 0.29 (95% CI, 0.07-0.53).
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. A small-to-moderate meta-analytic effect for restriction diets, with the conclusion that they benefit some children.

edges.quote: Omega-3 fatty acid supplementation, particularly with higher doses of eicosapentaenoic acid, was modestly effective in the treatment of ADHD.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Omega-3 is modestly effective and, per the same abstract, less so than standard pharmacotherapy.

edges.quote: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) comprises a deficit in behavioral inhibition. A theoretical model is constructed that links inhibition to 4 executive neuropsychological functions that appear to depend on it for their effective execution: (a) working memory, (b) self-regulation of affect-motivation-arousal, (c) internalization of speech, and (d) reconstitution (behavioral analysis and synthesis).
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). The foundational statement of the inhibition-centred executive-function theory of ADHD.

edges.quote: Groups with ADHD exhibited significant impairment on all EF tasks. Effect sizes for all measures fell in the medium range (.46-.69), but the strongest and most consistent effects were obtained on measures of response inhibition, vigilance, working memory, and planning.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Meta-analysis of 83 studies establishing which EF domains are impaired in ADHD and at what magnitude — the empirical content of the mechanism.

edges.quote: However, moderate effect sizes and lack of universality of EF deficits among individuals with ADHD suggest that EF weaknesses are neither necessary nor sufficient to cause all cases of ADHD.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. The crucial nuance against a single-EF-deficit account, and the empirical basis for the core-vs-one-component tension.

edges.quote: We conclude that EF ratings are better predictors of impairment in major life activities generally and occupational functioning specifically at adult follow-up than are EF tests.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Real-world EF ratings out-predict lab EF tests for adult impairment — extending the rating-vs-task dissociation into the ecological-validity domain.

edges.quote: Only 68 (24%) of the 286 relevant correlations reported in these studies were statistically significant, and the overall median correlation was only .19.
edges.rationale: Verbatim (verified against author-hosted full text; reused from the measurement note). Rating-based and task-based EF measures barely converge — method variance dominates, so a lab EF test and a real-world EF report are not interchangeable.

edges.quote: aerobic exercise had a moderate to large effect on core symptoms such as attention (SMD = 0.84), hyperactivity (SMD = 0.56) and impulsivity (SMD = 0.56)
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch); a clean clause of the results sentence. Meta-analytic effect sizes for aerobic exercise on the three core ADHD symptom domains in children/adolescents.

edges.quote: Cardio exercise seems acutely beneficial regarding various executive functions (e.g., impulsivity), response time and several physical measures.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Establishes the acute (post-bout) benefit of cardio exercise on executive functions and response time; the review also reports chronic benefits.

edges.quote: There was a significant effect of exercise on ADHD functional outcomes (g = 0.627).
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Pooled meta-analytic effect of exercise on ADHD functional outcomes (executive functions, motor skills).

edges.quote: Results suggest that exercise has a modest positive impact on ADHD functional outcomes, such as executive functions and motor skills, with longer interventions yielding better results.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. The honest magnitude and dose-dependence — modest, better with longer interventions — supporting the adjunct-not-replacement framing.

edges.quote: There is a growing body of literature showing that sex hormones have the ability to regulate intracellular signaling systems that are thought to be abnormal in ADHD.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). Gives the mechanism a substrate — sex hormones regulate the very signalling systems implicated in ADHD.

edges.quote: this functional interaction between sex hormones and molecules involved with synaptic plasticity and neurotransmitter systems may be associated with some of the clinical characteristics of women with ADHD.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Links hormone-neurotransmitter interaction to the clinical presentation of ADHD in women.

edges.quote: Research advances and future directions in female ADHD: the lifelong interplay of hormonal fluctuations with mood, cognition, and disease
edges.rationale: Verbatim article title (Eunethydis Special Interest Group review). States the lifespan framing — hormonal fluctuations interacting with mood and cognition throughout life.

edges.quote: Therefore, ADHD symptoms may change across the menstrual cycle in response to endogenous steroid changes.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (reused from the women-and-girls note). The menstrual-cycle instance of the broader lifespan modulation; medium given the small daily-diary sample.

edges.quote: The prevalence of PMDD and PPD were high in ADHD, compared to the general population.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract; PMDD = premenstrual dysphoric disorder, PPD = postpartum depression. Both elevated in women with ADHD versus the general population.

edges.quote: Adults with ADHD often report episodes of long-lasting, highly focused attention, a surprising report given their tendency to be distracted by irrelevant information. This has been colloquially termed "hyperfocus" (HF).
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). States the paradox that defines the mechanism — intense sustained focus in a disorder of distractibility.

edges.quote: Those with higher ADHD symptomology reported higher total and dispositional HF and more frequent HF across each of the three settings (school, hobbies, and screen time) as well as on a fourth subscale describing real-world HF scenarios.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Across a pilot and replication sample, self-reported hyperfocus rises with ADHD symptom level — the primary empirical support.

edges.quote: Hyperfocusing is higher in adult ADHD and there was no difference between stimulant-naive patients or patients on stimulants. Hyperfocusing can be defined as a separate dimension of adult ADHD.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Case-control evidence that hyperfocusing is elevated in ADHD versus controls and a separable dimension, independent of stimulant use.

edges.quote: Patients with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) suffer not only from inability to focus but also from inability to shift attention for events that trigger their interests.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. The reframe: ADHD involves failure to shift attention as well as to hold it — a regulation problem, not a simple shortage.

edges.quote: 'Hyperfocus' is a phenomenon that reflects one's complete absorption in a task, to a point where a person appears to completely ignore or 'tune out' everything else.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the open-access Psychological Research abstract (PMC7851038). A careful definition of the phenomenon the mechanism names.

edges.quote: Hyperfocus is most often mentioned in the context of autism, schizophrenia, and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, but research into its effect on cognitive and neural functioning is limited.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. The honest counterweight: hyperfocus is not ADHD-specific (also autism and schizophrenia) and the research base is limited — so 'elevated in ADHD' rests on young, non-specific evidence.

edges.quote: it has been suggested that impulsivity is not a unitary construct, but encompasses a variety of related phenomena that may differ in their biological basis.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). The core claim that impulsivity fractionates into components with different biological bases.

edges.quote: the field needs a domain-general construct of SR that encompasses SR of action, emotion, and cognition and involves both top-down and bottom-up regulatory processes.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract; SR = self-regulation. Situates impulsivity within a self-regulation that spans action, emotion and cognition — the framing that makes an emotional (urgency) facet part of the picture.

edges.quote: These findings provide robust evidence that delay discounting is significantly elevated among individuals with ADHD compared to controls.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (reused here for the choice-impulsivity facet). Meta-analytic evidence that ADHD steeply discounts delayed rewards — the delay-aversion/choice facet of impulsivity.

edges.quote: We found medium deficits in stop signal reaction time (SSRT), reflecting the speed of the inhibitory process, for attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) (g = 0.62), obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD) (g = 0.77) and schizophrenia (SCZ) (g = 0.69).
edges.rationale: Verbatim (reused from the measurement note). Stop-signal inhibition deficits of comparable size across ADHD, OCD and schizophrenia — the motor-impulsivity facet is real but not ADHD-specific.

edges.quote: Impulsivity, broadly defined as action without foresight, is a component of numerous psychiatric illnesses including attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), mania and substance abuse.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Names impulsivity as a component shared across ADHD, mania and substance abuse — transdiagnostic by definition.

edges.quote: Adolescents with a lifetime history of ADHD were at significantly higher risk of MDD through early adulthood relative to those with no history of ADHD.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). Establishes the elevated depression risk that co-occurrence rests on, in a large longitudinal school sample.

edges.quote: ADHD remained a significant predictor of MDD after controlling for gender, lifetime history of other psychiatric disorders in adolescence, social and academic impairment in adolescence, stress and coping in adolescence, and new onset of other psychiatric disorders through early adulthood (hazard ratio, 1.81; 95% confidence interval, 1.04, 3.06).
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. The prospective effect survives adjustment for a wide set of confounders, moving ADHD from correlate toward antecedent of later depression.

edges.quote: Our findings suggest that ADHD increases the risk of depression later in life and are consistent with a causal effect of ADHD genetic liability on subsequent major depression.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Mendelian-randomization plus cohort evidence for a partly causal ADHD to depression pathway — the strongest available support for the consequence reading.

edges.quote: As many as 80% of adults with ADHD have at least one coexisting psychiatric disorder
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the open-access BMC Psychiatry full text (PMC5567978); the review names mood and anxiety disorders among the most frequent. Reused here for the mood comorbidity; medium because it is an all-comorbidity figure, not depression-specific.

edges.quote: Attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is typically characterized as a disorder of inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity but there is increasing evidence of deficits in motivation.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). Establishes motivation as a third dimension of ADHD beyond the classic two — the mechanism this note names.

edges.quote: Using positron emission tomography (PET), we showed decreased function in the brain dopamine reward pathway in adults with ADHD, which, we hypothesized, could underlie the motivation deficits in this disorder.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Direct neurobiological evidence tying a motivation deficit to reduced dopamine reward-pathway function in adults with ADHD.

edges.quote: One of the core deficits in attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (AD/HD) is thought to be an aberrant sensitivity to reinforcement, such as reward and response cost.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. States the reinforcement-sensitivity account as a core-deficit candidate — the behavioural side of the reward story.

edges.quote: Results indicate that reinforcement contingencies have a positive impact on task performance and levels of motivation for both children with AD/HD and normal controls. There is evidence that the effect related to task performance is somewhat more prominent in AD/HD.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Reward improves performance and motivation, somewhat more so in ADHD — the empirical basis for treating performance as contingency-dependent.

edges.quote: Children with AD/HD prefer immediate over delayed reward.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Connects the note to the existing delay-aversion mechanism — the timing side of altered reward processing.

edges.quote: Individuals with ADHD appear to respond differently to incentives than their peers. This could be due to a general altered sensitivity to reinforcers.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Qualitative evidence that incentive response differs in ADHD; medium confidence as the study is interview-based and the theme structure was largely shared across groups.

edges.quote: It is often part of psychotherapies for adults with attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). However, procrastination is officially not acknowledged as an ADHD-related symptom.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). Captures the gap this note turns on: procrastination is clinically central to ADHD yet absent from the formal criteria.

edges.quote: Procrastination is increasingly viewed as involving failures in self-regulation and volition, processes commonly regarded as executive functions.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Frames procrastination as executive/self-regulatory failure; the study found EF domains predicted academic procrastination.

edges.quote: Strong and consistent predictors of procrastination were task aversiveness, task delay, self-efficacy, and impulsiveness, as well as conscientiousness and its facets of self-control, distractibility, organization, and achievement motivation.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Meta-analytic predictors (impulsiveness, distractibility, task delay, low self-control) are precisely the ADHD cognitive profile.

edges.quote: These effects prove consistent with temporal motivation theory, an integrative hybrid of expectancy theory and hyperbolic discounting.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Ties procrastination to hyperbolic (delay) discounting — connecting it to the reward/delay-aversion mechanism already in the graph.

edges.quote: People who are sensitive to social rejection tend to anxiously expect, readily perceive, and overreact to it.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). The foundational definition of rejection sensitivity as a general cognitive-affective disposition — the validated construct underneath the ADHD label.

edges.quote: American psychiatrist William Dodson introduced the concept based on clinical experience with clients with ADHD.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the English MEDLINE abstract of a Dutch-language critical reflection. Documents that RSD originates in clinical anecdote, not validation research.

edges.quote: An aspect of emotional dysregulation which remains relatively unexplored in ADHD, is rejection sensitivity. In people who experience rejection sensitivity, perceived rejection and/or criticism can evoke extreme dysphoria.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the open-access PLOS ONE abstract. Places rejection sensitivity under ADHD emotional dysregulation and defines the dysphoria; medium confidence as the study is qualitative with five participants.

edges.quote: emotion dysregulation is prevalent in ADHD throughout the lifespan and is a major contributor to impairment.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (reused from the anxiety note). Establishes the well-evidenced parent construct — emotional dysregulation — under which rejection sensitivity sits; medium because Shaw concerns ED broadly, not rejection sensitivity specifically.

edges.quote: married adults with ADHD reported poorer overall marital adjustment on the Dyadic Adjustment Scale (DAS; Spanier, 1989) and more family dysfunction on the Family Assessment Device (FAD; Eptein, Baldwin, & Bishop, 1983) than control adults.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). Standardised-measure evidence that adults with ADHD have poorer marital and family functioning than controls.

edges.quote: parents of youths diagnosed with ADHD in childhood (n = 282) were more likely to divorce and had a shorter latency to divorce compared with parents of children without ADHD (n = 206).
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Higher divorce rate and shorter time-to-divorce among parents of youths with ADHD — the family-strain route, distinct from an adult partner's own ADHD.

edges.quote: Participants who reported clinically significant levels of both hyperactivity-impulsivity and inattentiveness (consistent with ADHD-C) had lower relationship quality than those whose self-reported symptoms indicated no ADHD diagnosis.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Young-adult evidence that ADHD symptom level tracks lower romantic relationship quality.

edges.quote: Emotion regulation problems and hostile relationship conflict mediated this association.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Identifies emotion-regulation problems and conflict as mediators of the ADHD-to-relationship-quality link, tying it to the emotional-dysregulation axis.

edges.quote: much research points toward adults with attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) having short-lived and discordant romantic relationships
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). A 2021 review's summary of the converging literature — the relationships of adults with ADHD are shorter-lived and more discordant — giving the couple-strain finding review-level weight beyond the individual studies.

edges.quote: Analyses revealed greater negativity and less positivity in C-couples' behavior during a conflict resolution task, relative to IA and ND couples, and this corresponded with couples' relational satisfaction.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Directly coded conflict behaviour: combined-type (C) couples were more negative and less positive than inattentive (IA) and non-diagnosed (ND) couples, and this tracked satisfaction — locating the observable conflict signature in the combined presentation.

edges.quote: We found that 39% of the male and 43% of the female ADHD patients had symptoms of a sexual dysfunction, and 17% of the male and 5% of the female ADHD patients had symptoms of any other sexual disorder.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). Clinic-sample prevalence of sexual dysfunction well above general-population rates in both sexes — an intimacy strand of relationship impairment distinct from conflict.

edges.quote: Higher levels of ADHD symptomology in college students were related to increased social impairment and higher levels of state and trait anger, but not romantic relationship satisfaction or rates of IPV.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Supports the emotional-dysregulation route (ADHD symptomology tracks state/trait anger and social impairment) while itself finding no association with romantic-relationship satisfaction or IPV — the null half feeds tension:adhd-relationship-effect-not-universal.

edges.quote: Our results indicated a small significant relationship between media use and ADHD-related behaviors (r+ = .12).
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). Meta-analysis of 45 studies giving a small pooled correlation between media use and ADHD-related behaviors.

edges.quote: The available evidence suggests a statistically small relationship between media and ADHD-related behaviors.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Four-decade systematic review converging on the same small-magnitude conclusion.

edges.quote: Among adolescents followed up over 2 years, there was a statistically significant but modest association between higher frequency of digital media use and subsequent symptoms of ADHD.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Prospective cohort adding a temporal element, but the association is explicitly modest.

edges.quote: Further research is needed to determine whether this association is causal.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Even the prospective study declines to claim causation.

edges.quote: the extent to which screen media use and ADHD are linked remains a point of debate.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. The review's framing that the screen-ADHD link — including its direction — is still contested, motivating the call for causal research.

edges.quote: ADHD subjects revealed lower scores on all self-esteem domains compared to controls.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the open-access abstract. Case-control evidence that self-esteem is lower across all domains in children/adolescents with ADHD — the content of the mechanism.

edges.quote: Individuals with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) often grow up with negative messages surrounding their abilities and may experience adverse outcomes throughout their lives.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. States the accumulation account — negative messages over development — that frames low self-esteem as built rather than intrinsic.

edges.quote: there is evidence to suggest that ADHD is associated with lower self-esteem in adulthood and that self-esteem difficulties can be remedied, to at least some extent, by psychotherapeutic work.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Systematic-review conclusion of lower self-esteem in adults with ADHD (and its partial remediability).

edges.quote: Untreated ADHD was associated with poorer long-term self-esteem and social function outcomes compared with non-ADHD controls.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Long-term systematic-review evidence (127 studies) that untreated ADHD predicts poorer self-esteem outcomes.

edges.quote: Treatment for ADHD was associated with improvement in outcomes; however, further long-term outcome studies are needed.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Treatment was linked to improvement in most self-esteem outcomes — the modifiability point — with an appropriate caveat about the evidence.

edges.quote: Adults with ADHD had more autistic symptoms, and they had both more hyper- and hyposensitivity compared to norm groups.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). Establishes the bidirectional (hyper and hypo) sensory atypicality in adult ADHD relative to norms — the content of the mechanism.

edges.quote: Atypical sensory profiles as core features of adult ADHD, irrespective of autistic symptoms
edges.rationale: Verbatim article title. States the study's central conclusion that sensory atypicality is a feature of adult ADHD independent of autistic symptoms, not merely autism comorbidity.

edges.quote: Sensory processing problems in children with ADHD are more common than in typically developing children.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the open-access Psychiatry Investigation abstract (PMC3149116). Systematic-review conclusion that sensory problems are elevated in ADHD children versus controls.

edges.quote: Sensory processing problems in children with ADHD is not a well studied area.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. The honest counterweight: the evidence base is thin, so treating sensory difficulty as an established ADHD phenotype feature is premature.

edges.quote: Results showed a highly significant positive correlation between the number of ADHD traits and the frequency of reported sensory processing problems.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. General-population evidence that sensory difficulty scales with ADHD-trait level — the dimensional strand.

edges.quote: Our results suggest that sensory difficulties could be part of the ADHD phenotype.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Proposes sensory difficulty as part of the ADHD phenotype; medium confidence given the tentative 'could be' and the questionnaire, general-population design.

edges.quote: Intervention compared with control families reported a greater decrease in ADHD symptoms at three and six months (adjusted mean difference for change in symptom severity -2.9, 95% confidence interval -5.5 to -0.3, P=0.03, effect size -0.3, and -3.7, -6.1 to -1.2, P=0.004, effect size -0.4, respectively).
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). RCT evidence that a behavioural sleep intervention reduced ADHD symptom severity at 3 and 6 months versus usual care.

edges.quote: Current guidelines recommend assessment of sleep disturbance during evaluation of ADHD, and before initiation of pharmacotherapy, with healthy sleep practices the first-line option for addressing sleep problems.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (reused from the sleep note). Guideline framing that sleep hygiene is the first-line response to sleep problems in ADHD; medium as it states recommendation rather than an outcome.

edges.quote: Sleep onset advanced by 26.9 +/- 47.8 minutes with melatonin and delayed by 10.5 +/- 37.4 minutes with placebo (p < .0001).
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. RCT evidence that melatonin advances sleep onset in children with ADHD and sleep-onset insomnia.

edges.quote: The relationships of ADHD with sleep problems, psychiatric comorbidities and medications are complex and multidirectional.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). States the relationship is multidirectional, not a one-way mimic — the premise of the bidirectional hypothesis. (A separate Hvolby quote already supports the rival-boundary hypothesis in the arousal note.)

edges.quote: ADHD is either the cause or the consequence of sleep disturbances, or they may have a shared etiological and genetic background.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Names all three directions explicitly — cause, consequence, shared background — the core of both the bidirectional hypothesis and the sleep tension.

edges.quote: These findings demonstrate diurnal rhythm deviations during everyday life in the majority of adults with ADHD that have SOI
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract; SOI = sleep-onset insomnia. Objective actigraphy/melatonin evidence of circadian phase delay in most adult ADHD+insomnia — the empirical basis for the intrinsic-delay reading.

edges.quote: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is highly associated with the delayed sleep phase disorder, a circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorder, which is prevalent in 73-78% of children and adults with ADHD.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Puts a prevalence figure on delayed sleep phase in ADHD — high enough that it is hard to dismiss as incidental comorbidity.

edges.quote: We propose a novel view on ADHD, where a part of the ADHD symptoms are the result of chronic sleep disorders, with most evidence for the delayed circadian rhythm as the underlying mechanism.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Names delayed circadian rhythm as a proposed underlying mechanism for part of ADHD; medium because it is an explicit proposal ('we propose'), not a settled finding.

edges.quote: patients suffering from ADHD are at high risk to be confronted with stigma, prejudices, and discrimination.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). Review-level statement that ADHD carries a high risk of stigma, prejudice and discrimination.

edges.quote: individuals of all ages who exhibit symptoms of ADHD are the recipients of substantial stigmatization.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Developmental review finding substantial stigmatization across the lifespan, from multiple study types.

edges.quote: Most frequently perceived stereotypes were doubts about the validity of ADHD as a mental disorder.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Identifies validity-doubt as the leading ADHD stereotype — the factual claim the notebook's dimensional/genetic evidence contradicts.

edges.quote: The sample comprised n = 104 adults with ADHD, of whom n = 24 (23.3%) reported high internalized stigma, n = 92 (88.5%) anticipated discrimination in daily life and n = 70 (69.3%) perceived public stigma.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Prevalence of internalized stigma, anticipated discrimination and perceived public stigma among adults with ADHD.

edges.quote: The review demonstrates that ADHD patients are consistently impaired in three major timing domains, in motor timing, perceptual timing and temporal foresight, comprising several timeframes spanning milliseconds, seconds, minutes and longer intervals up to years.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). An integrative review's summary that timing impairment in ADHD is consistent across domains and timescales — the core empirical support.

edges.quote: While further replication is needed, growing evidence links ADHD to problems in several aspects of temporal information processing, including duration discrimination, duration reproduction, and finger tapping.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Names the specific temporal-processing tasks impaired in ADHD (the mechanism's content) while explicitly flagging that the evidence still needs replication — the caveat carried into the marker tension.

edges.quote: individuals with ADHD have difficulties in time estimation and discrimination activities as well as having the feeling that time is passing by without them being able to complete tasks accurately and well.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the open-access Med Sci Monit review. Links the measured estimation/discrimination deficits to the lived 'time blindness' experience.

edges.quote: This review summarizes recent research on the perception of time in ADHD and proposes that this symptom is a possible diagnostic characteristic.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. States the diagnostic-marker proposal explicitly; medium confidence because it is the authors' proposal, and timing deficits are not specific to ADHD (see the tension).

edges.quote: Working memory has assumed a prominent role as a primary neurocognitive deficit or endophenotype in extant models of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD).
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). States working memory's central place in ADHD models — the reason it is worth a dedicated treatment.

edges.quote: These findings suggest that children with ADHD exhibit statistically significant, large magnitude working memory deficits relative to their typically developing peers.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Meta-analytic magnitude of the deficit — large, across phonological and visuospatial domains.

edges.quote: Overall effect sizes for spatial storage (effect size = 0.85, CI = 0.62 - 1.08) and spatial central executive WM (effect size = 1.06, confidence interval = 0.72-1.39) were greater than those obtained for verbal storage (effect size = 0.47, confidence interval = 0.36-0.59) and verbal central executive WM (effect size = 0.43, confidence interval = 0.24-0.62).
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Gives the deficit profile — spatial working memory more impaired than verbal — a detail that shapes what tasks reveal it.

edges.quote: Children with ADHD exhibited deficits in multiple components of WM that were independent of comorbidity with language learning disorders and weaknesses in general intellectual ability.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. The deficit is robust — not an artefact of comorbid learning disorder or low IQ.

edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. First adult meta-analysis — the deficit is not outgrown, and inconsistent detection reflects method variance, relevant to an adult evaluation.

edges.quote: higher rates of activity level predicted significantly better, but not normalized WM performance for children with ADHD. Conversely, higher rates of activity level predicted somewhat lower WM performance for TD children.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. The compensatory result — movement helps working memory in ADHD but hinders it in typically developing children (TD).

edges.quote: As many as 80% of adults with ADHD have at least one coexisting psychiatric disorder
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the open-access BMC Psychiatry full text (PMC5567978), reused here as the headline comorbidity figure — most adults with ADHD have a co-occurring disorder.

edges.quote: Adult ADHD was highly comorbid with many other DSM-IV disorders assessed in the survey and was associated with substantial role impairment.

edges.quote: Children with ADHD were also more likely to develop disorders of abuse/dependence for nicotine, alcohol, marijuana, cocaine, and other substances (i.e., unspecified).
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Prospective meta-analytic evidence that childhood ADHD raises risk of later substance abuse/dependence across drug classes.

edges.quote: Overall, 23.1% (CI: 19.4-27.2%) of all SUD subjects met DSM-criteria for comorbid ADHD.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. The reciprocal direction — ADHD is present in roughly a quarter of substance-use-disorder patients — establishing the two-way link.

edges.quote: Girls and women with ADHD show a predominance of inattention and associated internalizing problems; boys and men display greater levels of hyperactive-impulsive symptoms and associated externalizing problems.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract; a distinct quote from this paper's existing triples. The inattentive/internalizing female profile is the mechanism of under-referral — less disruptive, so less likely to be flagged.

edges.quote: Females with ADHD experience, on average, serious impairments, with a particularly heightened risk for problems in close relationships and engagement in self-harm.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract; a distinct quote from this paper's existing triples. A review-level restatement that self-harm risk is heightened in females with ADHD.

edges.quote: Therefore, ADHD symptoms may change across the menstrual cycle in response to endogenous steroid changes.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Direct statement of hormone-linked symptom variation; medium confidence given the small daily-diary sample (N=32).

edges.quote: decreased levels of E2 in the context of increased levels of either P4 or T was associated with higher ADHD symptoms on the following day, particularly for those with high trait impulsivity.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract; E2 = estradiol, P4 = progesterone, T = testosterone. Specifies the hormonal pattern that tracks worse next-day symptoms — the mechanism's content. Medium confidence (single small study).

edges.quote: When amphetamine was given, the group showed a marked decrease in motor activity and reaction time and improved performance on cognitive tests.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). The 'group' is 14 normal (non-hyperactive) prepubertal boys — they improve on stimulants just as hyperactive children do.

edges.quote: evidence from this meta-analysis supports methylphenidate in children and adolescents, and amphetamines in adults, as preferred first-choice medications for the short-term treatment of ADHD.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Network meta-analysis of 133 RCTs — the strongest efficacy evidence for ADHD medication, with an adult-specific first choice.

edges.quote: Current CBTs for adult ADHD show comparable effect sizes to behavioral treatments for children with ADHD, which are considered well-established treatments.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Meta-analysis of 32 studies; establishes CBT as an efficacious non-pharmacological option for adults, not just medication.

edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Moderate effect sizes (inattention d = -.66; hyperactivity/impulsivity d = -.53) but the authors' 'possible benefits' wording is deliberately tentative — hence medium confidence.

edges.quote: spontaneous patterns of very low frequency (<0.1 Hz) coherence within a specific brain network ('default-mode network') thought to support a pattern of generalized task-non-specific cognition during rest, can persist or intrude into periods of active task-specific processing, producing periodic fluctuations in attention that compete with goal-directed activity.

edges.quote: The volumes of the accumbens (Cohen's d=-0·15), amygdala (d=-0·19), caudate (d=-0·11), hippocampus (d=-0·11), putamen (d=-0·14), and intracranial volume (d=-0·10) were smaller in individuals with ADHD compared with controls in the mega-analysis.

edges.quote: Parent report was more diagnostically sensitive than self-report. Young adults with ADHD tended to underreport current symptoms, while young adults without ADHD tended to overreport symptoms.

edges.quote: Unexpectedly, the childhood-ADHD and adult-ADHD groups comprised virtually non-overlapping sets; 90% of adult-ADHD cases lacked a history of childhood ADHD. edges.rationale: Verified against the PMC author manuscript. The strongest evidence AGAINST the late-identification reading — if adult cases carried childhood ADHD's polygenic risk, masking would predict it; they did not.

edges.quote: Among 166 individuals with adult ADHD, 112 (67.5%) did not meet criteria for ADHD at any assessment in childhood.
edges.rationale: Verified against the JAMA Psychiatry full article; independent cohort replicating the non-overlap finding that the late-identification hypothesis must explain away.

edges.quote: The findings of this study do not support the assumption that adulthood ADHD is necessarily a continuation of childhood ADHD. Rather, they suggest the existence of 2 syndromes that have distinct developmental trajectories.

edges.quote: Since symptoms were likely present but mitigated in childhood, these individuals might better be characterized as late-identified, rather than late-onset, ADHD cases

edges.quote: approximately 95% of case subjects who initially screened positive for late-onset ADHD were excluded from diagnosis

edges.rationale: Verified full text; refutes the persist/remit dichotomy and grounds person-environment fit as the evaluative frame.

edges.rationale: Verified against the fetched PDF; a 2.6x prevalence swing driven purely by whether childhood onset is required — definitional, not empirical.

edges.quote: Among these children, 303 (18.5%) of the males with elevated symptoms, and 111 (12.1%) of the females with elevated symptoms had an ADHD diagnosis recorded in the NPR.

edges.quote: As well, symptom lists for ADHD are biased toward male behaviors (e.g., physical overactivity or extreme risk-taking) as opposed to female-related manifestations (e.g., excessive verbalizations or more subtle indicators of impulsivity; see Quinn & Madhoo, 2014; Young et al., 2020).
edges.rationale: Verified full-text PDF; the instrument itself carries a reference-sample bias, another reason a single rating score is a weak anchor.

edges.quote: Analyses of diagnostic subtypes indicated that the predominantly inattentive type is the most common subtype in the population, but individuals with the combined type are more likely to be referred for clinical services.
edges.rationale: Verified against the Springer abstract; the structural referral filter that removes quiet presentations regardless of sex.

edges.quote: The arousal and activation are affected from a number of external and internal factors, such as availability of environmental stimulation, stress, sleep-wake cycle, noise, and, medications.
edges.rationale: Verified against the Ghent dissertation PDF (sic on 'affected from'). The energetic pools are defined as sleep- and stress-sensitive, so the mimics move the same variable by construction — the basis for the confounds edges.

edges.quote: the underlying impairment in ADHD is associated with the ability to self-regulate arousal rather than having a constant under or over aroused physiological state
edges.rationale: Verified against Frontiers full text; locates the putatively ADHD-specific element in regulation rather than level. Medium because the same authors note the evidence 'continue[s] to show mixed results'.

edges.rationale: Verified via PubMed abstract; positions state regulation upstream of the inhibition findings. Medium because the same abstract concedes the model needs direct measures of the energetic pools.

edges.quote: We propose that altered deactivation of the default mode network, and dysfunctional interaction with the executive control network, leads to excessive and spontaneous MW, which underpins symptoms and impairments of ADHD.
edges.rationale: Verified against PMC full text; the mechanistic proposal defining the mind-wandering axis.

edges.rationale: Verified against the Sage PDF. Medium because the increment was small in the comorbidity-free sample (R2 delta = .024) and much larger only where anxiety/depression co-occurred.

edges.quote: Our results suggest MW is associated with anxiety levels, independently of an ADHD diagnosis.
edges.rationale: Verified against the author-hosted PDF; the specificity failure. Medium because the sample was small (n=78 adolescents) and underpowered.

edges.quote: However, MW has been also associated with different developmental stages (Maillet et al., 2018), medication use (Raymond et al., 2019) and even Alzheimer's disease (El Haj et al., 2019) and cannot be considered a 'hallmark' of ADHD.
edges.rationale: Verified full text; the explicit non-specificity claim against the mind-wandering mechanism.

edges.quote: No experimental study has yet shown that sleep restriction induces hyperactivity, impulsivity or externalizing behaviors in children (Beebe 2011), despite the perception that 'paradoxical' hyperactivity exists as a behavioral response to daytime sleepiness
edges.rationale: Verified against PMC full text; the boundary that narrows the sleep rival to the inattention half of the picture.

edges.quote: a cumulative restriction of sleep of 54.04 minutes was associated with detectable deterioration
edges.rationale: Verified full text; experimental demonstration that modest sleep restriction degrades behaviour in children with no prior sleep or behavioural problems — the mimic shown causally.

edges.quote: To differentiate between ADHD and clinical anxiety, assessors may benefit from specifically asking patients whether restlessness, problems relaxing, and feeling driven by a motor are still present in the absence of clinical anxiety symptoms or prior to onset of an anxiety or related disorder.
edges.rationale: Verified against PMC full text; the counterfactual and temporal test — the concrete method for attacking tension:adhd-vs-anxiety-internal-restlessness.

edges.quote: The ADHD item having difficulty unwinding or relaxing (item within the factor of Hyperactivity) demonstrated poor specificity with measures of generalized anxiety.
edges.rationale: Verified full text; identifies the single worst-behaving item — and it is precisely an internal-restlessness item.

edges.quote: a) consider the age of onset of the symptoms (for example, when disentangling inattention as part of ADHD versus a mild chronic depressive disorder, the occurrence of inattentive symptoms before the onset of any mood symptoms reinforces the ADHD diagnosis); b) examine the trajectory of the symptoms (for example, the clearly episodic occurrence of hyperactivity, impulsivity and irritability can suggest bipolar disorder); and c) assess if the way symptoms manifest is better explained by another mental disorder
edges.rationale: Verified against PMC full text; the three structural tests generalised — onset, trajectory, mechanism.

edges.quote: Thus, hyperactivity in adults often manifests as inner restlessness, overscheduling, or not being able to relax properly.
edges.rationale: Verified full text; establishes that inner restlessness is a recognised adult manifestation of ADHD hyperactivity, so the personal hypothesis is at least well-formed. Medium and deliberately weak: this is a general clinical description, not evidence about this case, and the same mechanism has three standing confounds edges.

edges.quote: We found medium deficits in stop signal reaction time (SSRT), reflecting the speed of the inhibitory process, for attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) (g = 0.62), obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD) (g = 0.77) and schizophrenia (SCZ) (g = 0.69).
edges.rationale: Verified via Europe PMC REST. OCD's inhibition deficit EXCEEDS ADHD's, so the stop-signal task cannot be an ADHD-specific marker — the strongest form of the non-specificity argument.

edges.quote: Evidence indicates both disorders co-occur with a high frequency, in 20-50% of children with ADHD meeting criteria for ASD and in 30-80% of ASD children meeting criteria for ADHD.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). Quantifies the bidirectional co-occurrence — the empirical basis for treating ADHD/ASD overlap as substantial, not incidental.

edges.quote: family and twin studies do provide support for the hypothesis that ADHD and ASD originate from partly similar familial/genetic factors.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. The etiological claim: co-occurrence is underwritten by partly shared genetic origins, not only overlapping symptoms.

edges.quote: ASD and ADHD have shared genetic heritability and are both associated with shared impairments in social functioning and executive functioning.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Independent statement of shared heritability plus shared social/executive impairment — the neurocognitive layer of the shared substrate.

edges.quote: The research on ASD and ADHD suggests some overlap between the two disorders yet enough differences to indicate that these conditions are sufficiently distinct to warrant separate diagnostic categories.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. The counterweight: overlap does not erase the clinical distinction — the two remain separate categories.

edges.quote: The DSM-IV had specified that an ASD diagnosis is an exclusion criterion for ADHD, thereby limiting research of this common clinical co-occurrence.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Documents the historical DSM-IV bar on dual diagnosis (lifted in DSM-5) and names the co-occurrence as common — context for why the overlap was under-studied.

edges.quote: both ASD and ADHD share some phenotypic similarities, but are characterized by distinct diagnostic criteria.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Corroborates that phenotypic similarity coexists with distinct diagnostic criteria — supporting the distinct-categories reading.

edges.quote: Taken together, these analyses suggested that ADHD is best modelled as a continuum in both children and adolescents, thus supporting the genetic and other evidence that suggests a dimensional structure and multifactorial aetiology.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the fetched open-access full text; the canonical review's summary conclusion across three ADHD taxometric studies (Haslam 2006; Marcus & Barry 2011).

edges.quote: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder does not appear to have a taxon.
edges.pageApprox: 'Lack of evidence for a discrete category', para 1
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the cfp.ca full text; a taxon is the formal signature of a real category boundary, and ADHD lacks one.

edges.quote: Taxometric analysis outcomes were more consistent with a categorical structure to the data in the group with ADHD and a dimensional structure in the typically developing group.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the PMC full text; the mandatory rival — a taxometric result recovering categorical (not dimensional) structure within the ADHD group.

edges.quote: Both studies suggest that the diagnosis of ADHD is the extreme of a continuous distribution of ADHD symptoms in the population and that the etiologic factors involved in the disorder also account for the full range of symptoms.

edges.rationale: Verbatim from the Nature full text; twin evidence that the same aetiology operates across the whole symptom range, not just at the tail.

edges.quote: Strong concordance with GWAS of quantitative population measures of ADHD symptoms supports that clinical diagnosis of ADHD is an extreme expression of continuous heritable traits.

edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MDPI full text; sub-threshold cases carry real impairment, undercutting the idea that the threshold separates impaired from unimpaired. Medium because it is a narrative review reporting a secondary meta-analysis.

edges.quote: In this systematic scoping review of 334 published studies in children and adolescents, convincing evidence was found that ADHD is overdiagnosed in children and adolescents. For individuals with milder symptoms in particular, the harms associated with an ADHD diagnosis may often outweigh the benefits.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the PMC full text; the counter-argument that a continuum does not license unbounded threshold-lowering — a clinically justified action threshold is still required.

edges.rationale: Verbatim from the open-access SickKids manuscript; states the continuum framing and the measurement rationale behind dimensional instruments like the SWAN.
